title: "Say it again, I'm recording": the complaint that turns into a pitch
summary: A short skit: someone starts a tense complaint, the other person hits record, and it turns into an over-the-top pitch. AI writes the script.
why: Blue Bear Creative's weekly social trends post for October 21, 2026 lists "Say it again, I'm recording" at heat level 3 of 4: a tense customer confrontation that turns into an over-the-top product pitch.
steps: Pick the thing being "complained" about. It can be your cooking, your tidy closet, your dog's fancy haircut, or something your business makes.
Use the main prompt to write a 20 to 30 second script with two parts: a tense opening line, then the twist into a gushing pitch.
Film it with a friend, partner or co-worker who agreed to be in it. One person holds up a phone and says "Say it again, I'm recording."
Cut straight from the serious face to the big pitch. Add on-screen text if the audio is hard to hear.

prompts.label: Main prompt: the skit script
prompts.text: Write a 25-second comedy skit for a short video. Two people. Person A walks up looking upset and says something that sounds like a complaint about [thing, for example "my lasagna"]. Person B calmly takes out a phone and says "Say it again, I'm recording." Person A then turns the complaint into an over-the-top, gushing pitch, like a TV commercial: how good it is, why everyone needs it. Write it as short lines with simple stage directions. Keep it friendly, with no shouting, insults or swearing. Give me 3 different versions.

prompts.label: Variation: family or roommates
prompts.text: Write 3 versions of the "Say it again, I'm recording" skit set at home with family or roommates. Each starts with what sounds like a serious complaint, like "We need to talk about the dishwasher", and turns into an over-the-top compliment about something the other person did, like how well they loaded it. Under 30 seconds each, short lines, clean and kind.

prompts.label: Variation: on-screen text only
prompts.text: I want to do the "Say it again, I'm recording" trend without speaking. Write 5 versions as on-screen text only, 3 or 4 short text cards each. Card 1 is a serious complaint about [thing], card 2 is "Say it again, I'm recording", and the last cards are an over-the-top rave. Keep each card under 10 words.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run a [type of business]. Write 3 versions of the "Say it again, I'm recording" skit for our social media, acted by our own staff. A staff member plays a "customer" who walks up looking annoyed, then turns the complaint into an over-the-top pitch for our real [product or service]. Only mention things that are true about it: [list 2 or 3 real features]. No prices, no discounts, no fake results, and don't present it as a real customer or a real review. Under 30 seconds each.

tips: Make it obvious it's a skit. Never film real customers or strangers for this, and don't present it as a real review.
The joke lives in the switch. Play the opening line completely straight, then go big.
Keep the pitch true. Exaggerate the energy, not the facts.
Business accounts should use the app's commercial sound library or their own audio.
